summary_paragraph: A 78-year-old male with a history of severe aortic stenosis, diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and chronic bronchitis was admitted for worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema. He had been discharged recently after treatment for right leg cellulitis. Evaluation revealed acute on chronic diastolic heart failure exacerbation, likely due to medication noncompliance, with associated cardiorenal syndrome and elevated creatinine. He was treated with intravenous furosemide twice daily for seven days, resulting in improved dyspnea, resolution of pulmonary edema, and return of creatinine to baseline. His atrial fibrillation remained rate-controlled, though digoxin was briefly held and warfarin dose increased due to subtherapeutic INR. He was discharged home with home health services on oral furosemide, warfarin, and other baseline medications, with instructions to monitor weight, continue compression stockings, and follow up for INR testing.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
Contact dermatitis and other eczema, unspecified cause
